claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 15 years old.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful information.

Next question: **Are you responsible for Alex's care?** For example, do you provide for their daily needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex's care. I provide for all their daily needs - food, clothes, everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: **Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** 

This won't affect whether you can *get* Child Benefit, but it may mean you need to pay a tax charge on it.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't have a partner, and my income is below £60,000 per year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have one child, Alex, aged 15
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- You are responsible for Alex's care and provide for all their daily needs
- Your income is below £60,000

This is excellent news - you appear to meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit!

Before I provide my final assessment, just one last question to ensure I have complete information: **Is Alex currently in full-time education, or are there any special circumstances I should know about?** For example, is Alex in hospital, in care, or living with someone else for any period of time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, there is one thing I should mention - Alex is fostered. I'm fostering them, but I don't get anything from the council for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that important detail! 

Just to make sure I understand your situation correctly: **When you say you don't get anything from the council, does that mean the local council is not paying you anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the local council isn't paying me anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm covering all those costs myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for providing all that information.

## Good News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit! ✓

Based on everything you've told me, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:
- Alex is 15 years old (under 16) and lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's care and provide for all their needs
- As a foster carer, you can claim Child Benefit **as long as the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance** - which you've confirmed is the case
- Since your income is below £60,000, you won't have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you should contact HMRC or apply online to start receiving your Child Benefit payments.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
